features.name: formal education level
features.description: Captures the level of formal computer science training the letter presents, including whether it exceeds the role's minimum qualification.

levels.descriptor: No clear relevant degree is shown, or the education stated is below a bachelor's-equivalent baseline.
Shows a bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background, meeting the minimum but not the preferred academic tier.
Shows a relevant master's degree, signaling stronger formal preparation than the minimum.
Shows a relevant doctoral degree, indicating the strongest formal academic credential in this pool.

features.evidence: 3, 5, or 7 years testing, maintaining, and launching software
features.name: relevant experience duration
features.description: Captures how much directly relevant post-degree software engineering experience the applicant claims.

levels.descriptor: No clear duration is given, or the letter suggests less than the role's baseline.
Shows roughly minimum-level experience, about 2 to 3 years of relevant software product work.
Shows solid mid-level experience, about 4 to 5 years in relevant engineering work.
Shows extensive experience, about 6 or more years in relevant engineering work.

features.name: production delivery scope
features.description: Captures the breadth of production systems the letter says the applicant has tested, maintained, or launched.

levels.descriptor: Production scope is unclear or limited, with no concrete evidence of owning launched systems.
Shows experience across 1 to 2 production services, enough to demonstrate some real delivery history.
Shows experience across 3 to 4 production services, indicating meaningful breadth of production exposure.
Shows experience across 5 or more production services, indicating broad repeated delivery in production environments.

features.evidence: Python is all over my recent work
features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how concretely and extensively the letter demonstrates Python as a working production language rather than a box checked for alignment.

levels.descriptor: No Python experience is mentioned.
Python is mentioned, but only briefly or without evidence of meaningful use.
Shows regular Python use in production services, tooling, automation, or prototypes.
Shows deep, production-grade Python use with signs of engineering rigor, such as typed or tested services, cross-team tooling, or central operational dependence.

features.evidence: shipping language-model features and evaluation scaffolding
features.name: AI deployment maturity
features.description: Captures whether the applicant shows hands-on experience building and operating AI functionality in real software rather than only expressing interest.

levels.descriptor: No AI or LLM experience is mentioned.
AI is mentioned only generically, or as interest, exposure, or limited experimentation.
Shows direct experience shipping AI or LLM-backed features in production or near-production settings.
Shows production AI experience plus operational maturity, such as trustworthiness, evaluation, correctness, or reliability constraints.

features.evidence: Python agents with Go services defining boundaries
features.name: agentic architecture ownership
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter shows experience designing agent-based systems, especially the division of responsibility between agents and backend infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic tooling or agent-based system design is mentioned.
Agents or automation are mentioned at a high level, but without architectural detail.
Shows direct ownership of agentic tooling with a concrete Python-agent and Go-backend setup.
Shows end-to-end agent architecture thinking, including bounded actions, permissions, contracts, auditability, or guardrails around agent behavior.

features.evidence: proper security assessments with threat models and code review
features.name: security assessment depth
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter demonstrates performing security reviews or assessments as part of engineering work.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment experience is shown.
Security review is mentioned vaguely, without clear methods or scope.
Shows concrete assessment work such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface mapping, or validating fixes.
Shows especially strong assessment depth, such as leading reviews of unfamiliar services, treating reviews as deliverable-driven engineering work, or verifying remediation end to end.

features.evidence: automated the intake and triage of vulnerability reports
features.name: vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures whether the letter provides direct evidence of building tooling to handle incoming vulnerability reports or related security response workflows.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability handling or triage automation is mentioned.
Automation for security toil is mentioned, but not clearly tied to vulnerability intake or triage.
Shows direct experience building tooling for vulnerability intake, triage, routing, prioritization, or deduplication.
Shows direct ownership of a vulnerability workflow transformation, with before-and-after detail or clear operational leverage from the automation.

features.evidence: replacing a crumbling heuristic with a clean algorithm
features.name: algorithmic problem-solving evidence
features.description: Captures how strongly the letter demonstrates data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering examples rather than generic claims.

levels.descriptor: No data-structure or algorithm evidence is shown.
Makes a general claim about liking or knowing algorithms, but gives little concrete proof.
Provides a specific example of using algorithms or data structures to improve a real system.
Provides a strong example where algorithmic thinking solved a difficult bottleneck, simplified a tangled system, or materially changed system behavior.

features.name: security credential rigor
features.description: Captures the strength of formal security credentials presented beyond ordinary software experience.

levels.descriptor: No formal security credential is mentioned.
Shows a baseline credential focused on fundamentals, such as Security+, indicating structured security study.
Shows an advanced hands-on credential, such as OSCP, indicating practical offensive or assessment capability.
Shows an advanced credential and explains what it required or validated, making the rigor and relevance especially clear.

features.name: offensive security practice
features.description: Captures evidence of ongoing adversarial practice outside ordinary development work, especially through CTFs or similar hands-on exercises.

levels.descriptor: No ongoing offensive-security practice is mentioned.
Mentions occasional or casual practice, but without evidence of sustained engagement.
Shows regular hands-on practice through CTFs, labs, or similar adversarial exercises.
Shows serious or high-performing offensive practice, such as strong CTF placements or a clearly sustained competitive standard.

features.evidence: writing the patch and sending it upstream
features.name: open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows public engineering contribution through patching, maintaining, or leading open-source work.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
Shows occasional patching or contribution to dependencies, but not ownership.
Shows maintenance or ownership of a public project, including reviews or releases.
Shows stewardship of an actively used project with outside users or contributors, clear release responsibility, or broader ecosystem impact.

features.evidence: built a replicated cache, rate limiter, or consensus-backed store
features.name: personal systems-building ambition
features.description: Captures the ambition and technical substance of self-directed projects the letter uses as evidence of engineering depth.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a modest personal utility or small app with limited technical depth.
Shows a substantive side project with meaningful systems concerns such as replication, failover, recovery, or storage design.
Shows an especially ambitious sustained project tackling hard systems problems such as distributed coordination, compaction, consensus, or fault tolerance.

features.evidence: make secure development the default rather than the exception
features.name: developer-enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter understands security engineering as helping developers work securely by default rather than merely policing or reviewing them.

levels.descriptor: Shows only generic interest in security, without a clear view of helping other engineers work securely.
Hints at reducing toil or helping teams, but the enablement mindset is not central.
Explicitly frames the work as making the secure path easier, more automatic, or less frictionful for developers.
Articulates a strong developer-enablement philosophy, such as defaults over documents, proactive assistance, or embedding security into the development lifecycle.

features.evidence: improvements there are inherited by every team downstream
features.name: platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures whether the letter is motivated by central infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams rather than staying local to one product.

levels.descriptor: No clear interest in central platform or organization-wide leverage is shown.
Mentions scale or infrastructure in general terms, but not the downstream leverage of foundational work.
Clearly expresses interest in foundational systems, internal tooling, or broad organizational impact.
Shows a sophisticated platform mindset, explicitly valuing compounding leverage, shared defaults, or capacity gains across many teams.

features.evidence: software that guards other software must be built to a higher standard
features.name: rigor-first engineering philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents security tooling as work that demands exceptional reliability, precision, and engineering discipline.

levels.descriptor: No distinctive philosophy about rigor, reliability, or engineering standards is expressed.
Mentions reliability or care in broad terms, but without a strong personal stance.
Presents a clear personal credo that security or foundational systems should be built to a higher standard.
Connects that rigor-first philosophy tightly to the role, showing a nuanced view of why dependable security tooling matters and how it should be built.

features.evidence: returned hours of expert attention to the team
features.name: impact articulation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter explains the effect of the applicant's work on team capacity, system behavior, or operational outcomes.

levels.descriptor: Lists responsibilities or technologies without explaining what changed because of the work.
Suggests benefit, but the outcome remains vague or implied.
Gives a clear before-and-after or operational result, such as a queue becoming routed, a bottleneck disappearing, or hours being saved.
Shows strong leverage-oriented impact articulation, tying the work to measurable capacity, broad downstream benefit, or a transformed operating model.

features.name: mechanical writing accuracy
features.description: Captures the degree to which spelling, typing, and basic sentence mechanics distract from the application.

levels.descriptor: Frequent mechanical errors are obvious and repeatedly distracting.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Only minor or occasional mechanical errors appear.
The letter is clean and essentially free of mechanical errors.

features.evidence: sentence fragments such as Design ownership of agentic tooling
features.name: prose coherence
features.description: Captures how smoothly the letter reads as a structured argument, separate from mere typo count.

levels.descriptor: The prose is fragmented, awkward, or difficult to follow as a coherent application.
The prose is understandable but feels list-like, repetitive, or mechanically assembled.
The prose has a clear structure and logical flow from fit to motivation to evidence.
The prose is especially well-shaped and persuasive, with a distinctive voice or a strong narrative through-line.
